question: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Random-walk anchor is spot: 2.65 on 2026-09-03, with the median 10-trading-day change in this series ~0. I shade the median a tick wider to 2.67 for three reasons: 2.60-2.65 is the tightest zone since 2007 so the change distribution is right-skewed; post-Labor-Day HY supply plus September seasonality is a mild widening technical; and the Sep 15-16 FOMC sits inside the window with ~66% odds of a 25bp HIKE, an unusual hawkish configuration under Warsh with inflation above target. Offsetting: credit has ignored the hawkish repricing entirely (2.87 on Jul 29 to 2.60 on Aug 28 as hike odds doubled), issuance is refinancing-dominated (a positive technical), and a hike is largely priced so only a hawkish surprise bites. OAS is a spread over Treasuries, so a hike per se is not mechanically widening. Dispersion dominates the call: two weeks of a slow-moving index quoted to 0.01. Upper escape (>3.505 = +86bp in ~10 sessions) priced at 1.5% via the Apr-2025/Mar-2020 gap mechanism; lower escape omitted as 1.745 is 59bp below the 2007 all-time low. No prediction market prices this contract.

Whether the resolver reads the Sep 18-dated print or the latest print available at the Sep 18 20:00Z timestamp (which would be Sep 17-dated) is not specified in the criteria text and is worth flagging.

STATUS QUO
- Absent a shock, the index has been oscillating in a 2.60-2.87 band since mid-July, with the last six sessions in 2.60-2.67. The status-quo outcome is a print in the low-to-mid 2.6s.

EVENTS INSIDE THE WINDOW
- August CPI release expected approximately Sep 10-11, 2026.
- FOMC meeting Sep 15-16, 2026; statement and decision Wednesday Sep 16, two sessions before the window closes (confirmed schedule, multiple outlets, Aug-Sep 2026).
- CME FedWatch odds of a 25bp HIKE at the September meeting rose from roughly 33% to roughly 66% after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks that inflation had not meaningfully improved (CNBC, 2026-08-31; Marketplace, 2026-08-31).

- Counter-view in the same coverage: softer July employment and retail sales support a hold, and some economists expect no consensus to hike (Marketplace / Chase, Aug 2026). Chase coverage frames the shift as driven by energy shocks.

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD WIDENING
- Level is in the tightest 5% of readings over the past 25 years; HY spreads cited around 260bp and IG around 78bp in recent buy-side commentary (Nuveen fixed income weekly; T. Rowe Price Q3 2026 piece). Tight starting points mechanically leave more room to widen than to tighten.
- September is seasonally the heaviest post-Labor-Day HY new-issue calendar and historically the weakest month for risk assets.
- Long-end rate pressure: 30-year Treasury yield briefly reached its highest level since 2007 on persistent inflation, fiscal deficits and heavy issuance; year-end 2026 10-year forecast range cited at 4.25-4.50% (Schwab / Nuveen, mid-2026).
- Named risks flagged by sell-side: instability in non-bank/private lending and growth of liability management exercises (AllianzGI 2026 HY outlook).

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD FLAT OR TIGHTER
- The index tightened 27bp between Jul 29 and Aug 28 while September hike odds doubled - credit has so far absorbed the hawkish repricing without widening.
- Buy-side commentary describes credit fundamentals as broadly supportive and notes spreads tightening despite rate volatility; HY returned +0.27% in the most recent weekly period cited (Nuveen).
- Majority of expected HY issuance is refinancing rather than net new leverage, described as a positive technical (AllianzGI).
- Carry is attractive in absolute terms: the ICE BofA US High Yield Index yield was 6.99% as of the Q2 2026 Calamos commentary (Seeking Alpha, 2026-09-04), supporting demand.
- OAS is a spread over duration-matched Treasuries, so a policy rate hike does not mechanically widen it; only a change in default/risk premium does.

calls.reasoning: Random walk is the right central model for a daily OAS series over ~10 business days, so the median sits at the last print (2.65 on 2026-09-03) plus a hair of upward drift. Two things push the center up marginally rather than down: the index is only ~5bp off its 52-week low (2.60 on Aug 28) and within ~30bp of post-2007 record tights, so mean reversion at the tight end is mildly upward; and the window contains a Sep 15-16 FOMC with a dot plot where a hike is roughly coin-flip priced (~57% after Warsh), amid a global bond selloff. Against that, the last two Septembers both saw the index tighten across the same calendar stretch (2024: 3.31 to 3.21; 2025: 2.88 to 2.71), demand for HY paper is absorbing a heavy post-Labor-Day calendar, and the stress so far is in yields not spreads. Dispersion: 10bd changes have run SD ~0.13 over the past year, but only ~0.08 in the calm last quarter; I used the higher, event-uplifted figure. The distribution is right-skewed - the 2.60 area has acted as a floor for 19 months and the all-time low is 2.33, while +50-100bp two-week widenings from tight levels are a real if rare occurrence (Apr 2025, Mar 2020, Aug 2011). Escape above 3.505 needs +85bp in ten sessions, which has happened roughly 1% of two-week windows over 20 years; priced at 1.5% for the live FOMC and energy-shock tail. Escape below 1.745 has no mechanism (60bp below the all-time low) and is omitted.

calls.reference_class: 10-business-day-ahead changes in the ICE BofA US High Yield OAS (BAMLH0A0HYM2) during 2026, applied to the last observed level

calls.reasoning: Last print 2.65 (2026-09-03); the series is a near-random walk over ten sessions (2026 median 10bd change -0.02, mean -0.01, SD ~0.11). The window holds 9 sessions (Sep 7 is Labor Day), containing August CPI (~Sep 10-11) and the Sep 15-16 FOMC, where a 25bp HIKE is ~60% priced after Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks. I place the median at 2.66, essentially spot and below all three runs, because their common upward nudge double-counts: the 2026 empirical drift is slightly negative, both prior Sep 3->18 windows tightened (-10bp, -17bp), and if the distribution is right-skewed the widening belongs in the tail, not in the median. The skew itself is well supported - 2.60 has floored the series for 19 months and the all-time low is 2.33, while spreads widen fast from rich levels - so mean (2.685) sits above median. Credit has absorbed the hawkish repricing so far (2.87 on Jul 29 -> 2.60 on Aug 28 as hike odds doubled), OAS is a spread over duration-matched Treasuries so a hike is not mechanically widening, and September refinancing-dominated supply is a benign technical. No market prices this quantity.
calls.reconciliation: Four disputes. (1) FACTUAL, settled: the '~57-66% FedWatch' and BofA's '~15bp priced for September' figures are not in conflict - 15/25 = 0.6 - so all three dossiers describe the same live-but-priced hike. (2) FACTUAL, unsettled but immaterial: Run 3 alone has Aug payrolls at +162k vs ~53k consensus; Runs 1-2 could not retrieve it and I have no web access this run, so I carry it as plausible-unverified. It cuts both ways (growth-supportive, hike-supportive) and does not move the center. (3) JUDGMENT, and where I depart from all three runs: every run shifted the median to 2.67 AND right-skewed the tail. That double-counts widening. Run 2's own same-calendar base rate (2024 -10bp, 2025 -17bp) and 2026's -0.02 median drift argue against upward drift; the near-52wk-low conditional supporting it is n=2. I keep the skew, return the median to 2.66, and let the mean (2.685) carry the widening case. (4) FACTUAL, settleable from the dossiers: Run 3's FOMC-window changes (+0.15/+0.20/-0.10/-0.05/+0.12) are comparable to, not larger than, the unconditional SD of 0.11, so Run 2's 0.34 width is unsupported and Run 3's 0.28 ignores the event premium; I take 0.30. Also unresolved and stated as such: whether resolution reads the Sep 17 or Sep 18-dated FRED print, given the ~1-business-day publication lag - worth ~3bp, absorbed by the dispersion. Escape mass of 1.5% above 3.505 (+86bp in 9 sessions, ~1% of 20-year two-week windows, mechanism = Apr-2025/Mar-2020-style gap) carried forward unchanged; no lower escape, as 1.745 is 60bp below the 1996-2026 all-time low.

disagreements.claim: The median should be nudged above spot to 2.67 on tight-end asymmetry and event density

Settled at 0.30. Full-2026 SD 0.11 x 2.56 = 0.28; FOMC-containing 2026 windows moved ~0.05-0.20, i.e. not larger than unconditional, so 0.34 is unsupported - 0.30 adds a modest event premium to the 0.28 anchor.
